title: Israel's military begins its ground offensive in Gaza City
body:
On 16 September 2025, the Israeli military launched the main phase of its offensive in Gaza City, according to an Associated Press report citing an anonymous Israeli military official. The military said it believed 2,000 to 3,000 Hamas militants remained in the city, along with tunnels the group uses. Israel pledged to take control of the entire city, gave no timeline, and Israeli media suggested the operation could take months. Defense Minister Israel Katz said: "Gaza is burning."

The Israeli military estimated that 350,000 people had left Gaza City, which had been home to about one million Palestinians before evacuation warnings. A UN estimate said more than 220,000 Palestinians fled northern Gaza over the previous month. Hospitals reported at least 69 deaths from strikes that Tuesday, and Shifa Hospital received 49 bodies, including 22 children. The Gaza Health Ministry said more than 64,900 Palestinians had been killed in the war and does not distinguish civilians from combatants.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned of a very short window of time in which a deal could happen. Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi called Israel an enemy, the first time an Egyptian leader had done so since the countries established ties in 1979. Of the 251 people abducted on 7 October 2023, 48 hostages remained in Gaza, fewer than half believed alive, and Israel believed around 20 were alive. Israel rejected a UN Human Rights Council expert finding of genocide issued the same day as distorted and false.
